findings.title: Proceeding when the webhook integration is absent bypasses installer validation
findings.body: The identity comparison is only performed after an Integration record with webhook-derived `metadata.sender` already exists. If the installation webhook is delayed, dropped, or has not yet been processed, this `Integration.DoesNotExist` branch advances to the creation step without any installer identity check. That creation step can fetch arbitrary Sentry GitHub App installation details using the app credential, so a Sentry org administrator who knows an installation ID can link an installation before its webhook record is available, even though their OAuth GitHub user was not the installer. Do not advance this path until an authenticated installation event has recorded the sender (or obtain an equivalent authoritative installer identity).

findings.title: Missing webhook sender metadata causes a 500 during reinstallation
findings.body: `sender` is not guaranteed to be present in Integration metadata: `build_integration` only persists it when a pipeline state supplies `sender`, while ordinary frontend-created integrations do not supply that state. If such an active integration remains after its OrganizationIntegration is removed, this is exactly the branch reached, and indexing `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError instead of returning the installation failure response. This blocks relinking/reinstalling affected existing integrations and exposes an internal error; safely handle absent or malformed sender metadata as a failed verification.
